card.title: Professional Suspicion
card.instruction: Treat inconsistencies, evasions, and missing details as evidence your trained eye should investigate before anyone proceeds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I approve your expenses: the receipt says four, your note says four-oh-five.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought a biscuit on the way back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then there's a second transaction missing from your account.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid for it myself. Here, have the other one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two biscuits. I'll need to revise the timeline before I sign.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 investigates a five-minute expense discrepancy, A3 turns the biscuit explanation into a missing transaction, and A5 treats a second biscuit as reason to reopen the timeline.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's biscuit stop supplies A3's transaction concern; B4's personal payment and spare biscuit cause A5's count-based revision.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains elapsed time and B4 clarifies it was not claimed as an expense while offering the spare.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's attempt to settle the matter as another detail requiring investigation before signature.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes an expense approval and conflicting receipt-note times.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's two-biscuits count is earned by B4's other-one offer, though the suspicion is disproportionate.
